title: An orphan in the desert
hookLine: his father dies before he is born, and no nurse wants the fatherless baby, until Halimah takes him to the desert

lines: A FATHER GONE BEFORE THE BIRTH.
cards: Before the boy was even born, his father was gone. 'Abdullah, a young man, had left on a trading journey, fell ill on the way home, and died. So Aminah gave birth to a son whose father would never hold him.
His grandfather named him Muhammad ﷺ. Meccan families had a custom: they sent their babies out to the desert tribes, to be nursed by Bedouin women, for the clean air and the pure Arabic.
Every so often, desert women came into town looking for babies to nurse, because the parents paid well. That year, not one of them wanted this baby. No father.

teach.b: Ibn Ishaq's biography tells it through one of those women: Halimah, of the tribe of Banu Sa'd. It was a drought year.
Her donkey was so weak it held up the whole group, and her own baby cried all night because she barely had milk. Every other woman found a child.

teach.h: SHE TAKES THE ONE LEFT OVER.
teach.b: Halimah found only the orphan. Rather than go home with nothing, she told her husband: I'll take him. The story says that from that night everything changed.
Her milk came in, their old camel gave milk, and her slow donkey ran ahead of the others. The orphan nobody wanted brought blessing into the tent.
He grew up out there for several years, running with the flocks, speaking the Arabic of the desert. Years later, the Qur'an would speak to him about this.

teach.h: DID HE NOT FIND THEE AN ORPHAN?
teach.b: In Surah Ad-Duha, in Pickthall's translation: “Did He not find thee an orphan and protect (thee)?”
And two verses later, the job that comes with it: “Therefor the orphan oppress not.” Orphans come up again and again in the Qur'an. Their property is to be guarded, not devoured.
They're to be fed, honored, never pushed away.
And a hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari says the Prophet ﷺ held up two fingers, side by side, and said that he and the one who cares for an orphan will be like this in Paradise.
The boy nobody wanted became the one who told the world to want them.

how: Islam asks believers to care for orphans; some Muslims sponsor an orphan through a charity, and Surah Ad-Duha is read as a reminder of the Prophet's own childhood.

games.q: you're Halimah, in a drought year. every other woman has found a baby to nurse. the only one left is an orphan whose family can't pay much. what do you do?
games.why: she takes him rather than go home empty-handed, and the story says her tent was blessed from that night on (Ibn Ishaq).

practice: Think of someone who's on their own right now: a widowed neighbor, a new kid at school, a coworker who eats lunch at their desk, someone far from family.
Picture their face, and choose one small thing that would tell them someone noticed, a knock on the door, a seat saved, a message. If you pray, you can ask Allah to shelter them.

wordCard.voice: Yatim. An orphan, a child who has lost a father. The Prophet ﷺ was one, and the Qur'an asks that every orphan be protected.

orig.note: Arabic: an orphan, especially a child who has lost a father.

carryVoice: Your line: Allah shelters the orphan. Tomorrow, the people who took him in, one after another. That's day eighty.
